correctness.rationale: The endpoint convolution norm equals the L1 norm of the central Peter–Weyl Dirichlet kernel. Differentiating the odd-frequency cosine sum gives K_L(theta)sin^2(theta)=-m cos(2m theta)+(cot(theta)/2)sin(2m theta), m=L+1. After half-period symmetry and u=2m theta, the deficit from 4m/pi is the finite integral of |cos u-b_m(u)sin u|-|cos u|, with b_m(u)=cot(u/(2m))/(2m). On compact u intervals b_m->1/u; uniformly controlled oscillatory tails use the bounded primitive of sin(u)sgn(cos u) and small sign-flip neighborhoods of cos zeros. This warrants the improper-limit exchange. The first pi-interval has Si(pi)-2<0 and later pi-interval defects are each negative by the given T_a/E_a inequalities and O(k^-2), so C_rot<0. I independently numerically integrated the exact finite-m formula for m=1,2,4,8,16,32,64: deficits approximately -0.27324,-0.18389,-0.14299,-0.12296,-0.11299,-0.10802,-0.10553, tending toward the claimed -0.10304. These samples corroborate, not prove, the all-L asymptotic. No interval-certified decimal or quantitative o(1) rate is asserted.

originality.rationale: The mathematical object is the L1 norm of an integer-spin (even-highest-weight on SU(2)) contiguous SO(3) Fourier projector, specifically its finite additive term. Existing rotation sampling, Cesaro summability and compact-group character norms concern different operators or weaker growth; the published Resultary SU(2) *full* cutoff gives a leading constant only and cannot transfer the absolute-value norm under parity restriction. The exact negative additive constant was not identified in the materially inspected sources. The inaccessible 1982 character-norm paper leaves a real priority risk, so this is a qualified best-of-knowledge rather than definitive global priority conclusion.

value.rationale: The exact two-term sharp endpoint norm describes quantitative amplification of the canonical non-Cesaro rotational Fourier truncation, a natural problem in harmonic analysis. An explicit, provably negative O(1) edge correction adds nontrivial information beyond the classical divergent leading term and is stable under a precisely specified normalization. The result is not a mere rounding of a known growth constant, and the limit integral and sign require oscillatory cancellation analysis.
